land.text: Pereyaslavl, which Vsevolod I received in Yaroslav's division (Kievan Rus' and Principality of Pereyaslavl pages); Cliopatria's first shape of this state is 1056

predecessors.note: The Pereyaslavl page's infobox says 'Established: 988' and its text 'from the end of 9th century until 1323'; the map draws the principality from the 1054 division, as the rus dossier ends then.

land.text: the principality's last Cliopatria shape, conquered in March 1239; inside Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape of 1241

successors.note: After 1239 'the territory was apparently abandoned and stayed uninhabited until the 15th century' (Pereyaslavl page); Algirdas acquired Pereyaslavl, with Chernigov and Kiev, 'around 1360'.

capitals.name: Pereyaslavl (Pereiaslav)
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Pereyaslavl, on the Trubizh; the city was destroyed in 1239.

correction.text: the 1056 shape: the left bank of the middle Dnieper east to the Seversky Donets side

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1054-1055: Cliopatria's first shape is 1056, but the Kievan Rus' page gives 'Principality of Pereyaslavl and Rostov-Suzdal, for Vsevolod I of Kiev' in the division 'after the death of Yaroslav I in 1054'. The 1056 shape is used.

94,900 km2 on the left bank of the middle Dnieper (30.6-38.7 E, 49.4-51.4 N). Page: the principality covered land 'from the left banks of the middle Dnieper on the west to an eastern frontier "not far west from the Seversky Donets"', with the city on the Trubizh. The infobox gives no area, so nothing to compare.

95,100 km2 for 1072-1235 (+205 km2, a handful of cells at the eastern edge). The page dates no frontier event in these years: 'usually administered by younger sons of the Grand Prince of Kiev'; the Cumans are named only in passing; Roman of Halych's hold on Pereyaslavl (1203-1205) is a vassal event in the galicia-volhynia dossier.

Same shape for 1236-1240. Pereyaslavl page: 'In March 1239, Pereyaslavl was conquered and devastated by the Mongols'; Mongol invasion page: 'In the winter of 1239, he sacked Chernigov and Pereyaslavl'; its inhabitants fled to north-eastern Rus'. Cliopatria ends the shape in 1240.

region.text: Pereyaslavl and the left bank of the middle Dnieper

ledger.note: 1054: Yaroslav's death gives Pereyaslavl, with Rostov-Suzdal, to his son Vsevolod I. Kievan Rus' page: 'Principality of Pereyaslavl and Rostov-Suzdal, for Vsevolod I of Kiev'; the Pereyaslavl page: 'Among Yaroslav's sons, Vsevolod received Pereyaslavl'. Yaroslav died on 20 February 1054 (Yaroslav the Wise page infobox). Cliopatria's shape begins in 1056.
March 1239: the Mongols attack Pereyaslavl. 'In March 1239, Pereyaslavl was conquered and devastated by the Mongols.'

March 1239: Pereyaslavl falls. The mongol-empire dossier records the principality as a Mongol vassal from 1239; the Mongol invasion page: its inhabitants fled 'to northeastern Russia immediately after the invasion'. After 1239 the territory 'was apparently abandoned and stayed uninhabited until the 15th century'.

1240: Cliopatria's last Pereyaslavl shape; from 1241 the land is inside the Mongol shape. The page's last dated event is the conquest of March 1239 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1239/1323'). Confidence 1: the year is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'
wars.outcome: Pereyaslavl is conquered and devastated in March 1239; the land lies empty for generations and Danylo of Halych is met by Tatars at Pereyaslavl in 1245 on his way to Batu Khan.
wars.note: The Mongol invasion page dates the sack of Chernigov and Pereyaslavl only to 'the winter of 1239'; the Pereyaslavl page gives March.

certainty.note: The steppe frontier on the south and east (Cumans) was never fixed by treaty or survey, and the Dnieper and forest edges are approximate; the page puts the eastern limit only 'not far west from the Seversky Donets'.

notes:
Start 1054 follows the Kievan Rus' page (division 'after the death of Yaroslav I in 1054') and the rus dossier; the Pereyaslavl infobox says 'Established: 988' and the text 'from the end of 9th century until 1323', and the Primary Chronicle dates the city's foundation to 992, none of which matters for the map. Page budget: Pereyaslavl and Mongol invasion (2), with the Kievan Rus' and Yaroslav the Wise pages shared with the other dossiers of this batch.

The Pereyaslavl page is thin: it lists no princes of the 1054-1240 years, does not mention the Cumans, the Alta (1068), Salnitsa (1111), 1183, 1185 or Kalka, or Chernigov's holdings, so the stretch 1056-1235 has no dated event beyond the founding. The shape is Cliopatria's; the area could not be compared (no infobox figure). Roman of Halych's vassalage over Pereyaslavl (1203-1205) is recorded by the principality-of-galicia-volhynia dossier (vassal events on the suzerain side) and not repeated here.

Mongol end: Cliopatria's shape runs to 1240, the conquest is March 1239; the dissolve is confidence 1 at 1240. The mongol-empire dossier carries contest and vassal_start events for Pereyaslavl in 1239. Region names needed: none.
